answer_1.quote: our work presents the first systematic investigation of how pruning affects fairness in LLM-generated summaries... We evaluate fairness across multiple pruning methods, various calibration sets, and four fairness metrics, ...

answer_2.quote: Performance: the quality of the generated summaries is evaluated through comparison with the corresponding reference summaries using two automatic evaluation metrics, ROUGE, an n-gram overlapping metric, and BERTScore, an embedding-based evaluation metric.

answer_4.quote: We conduct a systematic comparison of output fairness across five pruning methods using human evaluation... annotators identified distinct positive and negative opinions in each input, then assess which summary better preserves the original opinion distribution, achieving substantial inter-annotator agreement with a Fleiss' Kappa coefficient of 0.555.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to choose which summary better preserves the original opinion distribution (i.e., fairness of opinion representation).
